newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish police bust gay sex ring involving children.
newsitem.headline: Polish police bust gay sex ring involving children.

text.p: Police investigating the biggest paedophile ring ever uncovered in Poland said on Wednesday more than 100 foreigners were on the lists of a homosexual contacts service which offered under-age boys for sex.

Police Lieutenant Pawel Biedziak told Reuters the alleged organiser of the ring, a 44-year-old local government official in the northern city Szczecin, had been formally accused by police of sexual offences against minors.

The ring's existence was revealed on Tuesday by Polish public television's Wiadomosci news programme which showed explicit but electronically-blurred photographs, confiscated by police, of men and boys engaged in sexual activities.

Biedziak said police had raided the home of the civil defence inspector and former army officer, whom he identified only by the underworld alias "the Major", after being alerted by a journalist and a call to a helpline for abused children.
The police found a computer with nearly 1,000 names of men seeking gay sex partners. Most of these men were interested in other adults and Biedziak said they did not concern the police.

"But among the adults there was a part who specified they wanted to meet underage boys for sexual contacts and that will be the subject of our interest," said Biedziak, speaking by telephone from provincial police headquarters in Szczecin.
Biedziak said about 100 men on the lists were foreigners, but would not say how many were suspected of abusing minors.
He said none were from Belgium, which has been rocked this year by child-sex scandals.
The television said the men listed or named by boys were from the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, France, Austria, Canada, Slovakia, Ukraine, Russia, Belarus and Saudi Arabia.

The computer also contained names of boys, including more than a dozen elementary school pupils, who were available for sexual contacts with adults and usually were seeking a so-called "sponsor" who would support them financially.
Biedziak said the Szczecin police had started by tracing boys who featured on photographs found at the scene and several of these had said they had had sex with the Major.
"One of these boys also speaks of contacts, when below the age of 15, with a citizen of Sweden," Biedziak said.

The television news interviewed boys who had been under 15, the age above which sexual relations are not the subject of prosecution in Poland, when they were allegedly picked up by the Major at stations or video parlours and lured to his home.
One, 14-year-old Robert who was shown in silhouette, said he had telephoned the Major and been invited to meet a man.
"The guy said he was rich and so on. I didn't bother about that, I went and slept with him," said Robert.
Biedziak said the youngest boy confirmed to have been involved with the Major was 14. He stressed that the large-scale investigation was still in its early stages.
Following up its report on Wednesday, the television cited police and one of the boys as saying the Major had allegedly offered boys to brothels in Germany and encouraged them to go.
There has been public concern that child abusers from wealthy Western Europe may be coming to Poland to prey on children from deprived homes.

Warsaw police spokesman Andrzej Przemyski said the Szczecin case was by far the biggest of its kind uncovered in Poland, although there were continued cases of Polish boys travelling to Berlin to offer themselves for prostitution.
"It was a shock for us...it's the first such case in Poland (on this scale) and as far as I know, it is one of the biggest such cases in Europe," he told Reuters.
